C-39.Name: Tables: width, overflow and a fullscreen viewer
C-39.Summary: GFM has no notation for table or column width (the delimiter row only carries alignment; dash counts are a Pandoc-only convention, kramdown attributes and HTML colgroup are not portable). Mark renders tables with the browser's auto layout and no overflow handling (src/muya/themes/default.css:426-470, src/muya/lib/assets/styles/index.css:519), so a wide table or a long URL runs past the text column. This change defines good default rendering, a session-only manual column width, and a fullscreen viewer shared with the Mermaid viewer (C-34 R2.2).

Problem.Description: User question 2026-10-15: how is table and column width controlled, is there a notation, what should the default rendering be. Wide tables overflow the text column; one long URL inflates its column; there is no way to study a large table as a separate object.

Goals.R-1: Wide tables never overflow the text column: the table sits in a horizontally scrollable wrapper with an edge shadow on the side that has hidden columns.
Goals.R-2: Narrow tables keep content width (not stretched to the column) and sit centred in the text column like diagrams (user 2026-10-15, like MarkView); the table tools bar is centred over the table and the viewer's expand button sits beside the table's top-right corner; export/PDF centres tables too. Cell text alignment stays as the GFM delimiter row says.
Goals.R-3: Long unbreakable tokens (URLs, paths, hashes) wrap inside body cells (max cell width ≈ 40ch, overflow-wrap: anywhere); header cells and short words are not broken mid-word.
Goals.R-4: Fullscreen viewer for a table as a separate object (hover ⤢ button, same shortcut as diagrams): pan/zoom, sticky header, Esc closes, read-only. Built as ONE shared block-viewer overlay together with C-34 R2.2 (Mermaid), so both get the same controls and shortcuts.
Goals.R-5: Manual column width by dragging a column border; lives only for the session (not written to the .md, reset on reload); double-click the border resets to auto.
Goals.R-6: HTML/PDF export follows the same rules; in print/PDF wide tables wrap text instead of scrolling (no clipped columns).
Goals.R-7: P2: sticky header row for long tables in the editor.

T1.Title: Default rendering: overflow wrapper + edge shadows, content width, long-token wrap, export/PDF rules
T1.Acceptance: WebKit screenshots before/after on wide (15 columns), narrow (2×2) and long-URL tables, light and dark; the wrapper does not break table editing (cell focus, drag bars, table tools, selection across cells); PDF export of a wide table shows every column. Unit/e2e pins for the wrapper and the wrap rules.

T2.Title: Shared fullscreen block viewer (tables + Mermaid, with C-34 R2.2)
T2.Acceptance: One overlay component serves both block types; table view is read-only with pan/zoom and a sticky header; Esc returns focus to the block; e2e in Chromium and WebKit.

T3.Title: Session-only column resize
T3.Acceptance: Dragging a border changes the width live; the saved file is byte-identical; reload restores auto layout; double-click resets.

C-39.Dependencies: T2 is built together with C-34 R2.2. T1 starts after C-34 R2.1 is merged (both touch src/muya/lib/assets/styles/index.css).

Constraints.Constraint: No width notation is written into Markdown; files stay portable GFM.
Table editing (cell navigation, drag bars, table tools) keeps working inside the wrapper.
Works under the WKWebView CSP; no new IPC permissions.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Persisting column widths in the file (HTML colgroup, Pandoc dash widths, attribute syntax).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A 15-column table and a cell with a 200-character URL stay inside the text column in the editor and in PDF export; a 2×2 table keeps content width; a large table opens fullscreen and zooms like a Mermaid diagram.

AffectedAreas.M-011: muya table rendering (renderContainerBlock), table CSS in themes, export HTML/PDF styles, shared block viewer

C-39.VerificationIntent: WebKit screenshot matrix (wide/narrow/URL × light/dark), Playwright e2e for scroll/wrap/viewer, PDF export check, live check in the real app.
